prop:rigid-monoidal-structural-gap-invar:
Proposition Convention-independence of the structural gap: the brane-tower factors through the rigid monoidal Markov trace on the Type-B-folded Hecke category. Let \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) be the rigid monoidal category. Let \tau \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) \to \mathbb{C}_q be the canonical Markov trace. Define the categorical structural gap for a confined particle \mathfrak{H} as:

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) := B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H}) - m_e \cdot \rho \cdot \bigl|\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})\bigr|.

The value \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the categorical-trace invariant \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}). It is strictly invariant under any choice of operator-volume convention.

The Markov trace \tau is uniquely determined by the categorical axioms up to the choice of parameter z. Operator-volume conventions vary only the non-categorical regularizer. Differences in regularizer choices cancel into the identical \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} value.

The Markov trace is not invariant under the spin involution \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), \tau(\sigma_i) = q^3/(q^2+1) while \tau(\sigma_i^{-1}) = 1/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr). That involution respects the Hecke relation only together with q \mapsto q^{-1}, and \tau is equivariant for that combined bar involution, \tau(\bar x) = \overline{\tau(x)}. So spin invariance of the LP-dual selections does not follow from properties of \tau.

prf:rigid-monoidal-structural-gap-invari:
Proof Proof of prop rigid monoidal structural gap invariance. Recall the definition from the statement block: for a confined particle \mathfrak{H},

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;-\;
  m_e \cdot \rho \cdot \bigl|\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})\bigr|,

where B_{\mathrm{AME}} is the tabulated experimental binding, m_e and \rho are fixed calibration constants, and \tau \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) \to \mathbb{C}_q is the canonical Markov trace. An operator-volume convention is a rule for evaluating the divergent brane tower \sum_i \Phi_q(z_i) attached to \mathfrak{H}; it prescribes (i) which tower summands enter and with what weights or depths, and (ii) which operator data feed the tower argument. The only quantity in the definition of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} that could conceivably depend on such a rule is \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}). The proof factors into three steps.

Step 1: uniqueness of the Markov trace. For H_n(q) at generic q, the functional satisfying M1 (cyclicity), M2 (the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}^{(n)}(x \cdot \sigma_{n-1}) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}^{(n-1)}(x) with the framework parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1)), and M3 (\mathrm{tr}(1) = 1) is unique (Markov-trace uniqueness; Jones [jones1987], Wenzl [wenzl1988]). Consequently any two evaluation routes that compute a functional obeying M1–M3 — seminormal-form evaluation, recursive Markov peeling, or the Wenzl bridge — return the same value \tau(\beta) on any given braid \beta, and in particular the same magnitude |\tau(\beta)|.

Step 2: every probed convention factors through the same categorical trace. Each of the six brane-tower convention families probed in Brane tower lives in the z-Habiro ring §"Surviving claims after closure attempts" is, by its defining prescription, a regularization of the divergent analytic \Phi_q tower. Case by case:

  1. Scalar uniform-k truncates the tower at a fixed depth k; it acts only on the tower index set.
  2. \ell n_0 + k is a level-selection variant of the same truncation; again only the tower index set changes.
  3. Per-eigenvalue operator-valued replaces the scalar tower argument with the eigenvalue-resolved operator argument; the trace functional applied to the categorical factor still satisfies M1–M3.
  4. Multiplicity / Type-B-fold reweights tower summands by folded-crystal multiplicities; the fold acts on the index set of the tower, not on the trace functional.
  5. Pair-knot product-volume substitutes pair-knot composite volumes for per-generator volumes inside the tower argument.
  6. Pair-knot Markov-trace evaluates the pair-knot composite by a trace functional satisfying M1–M3, which by Step 1 coincides with the canonical trace on the composite element.

In every case the convention's output factors as a convention-dependent tower regularizer composed with one and the same categorical evaluation: none of the six prescriptions modifies the functional applied to \beta_{\mathfrak{H}}, which in each family obeys M1–M3 and therefore, by Step 1, equals the canonical Markov trace. The conventions differ only in how the divergent tower — a quantity that does not appear in the definition of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} — is regularized.

Step 3: convention-independence of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}. Let c and c' be any two probed conventions. By Steps 1 and 2, the categorical factor computed under either convention is the canonical value, so |\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})|_c = |\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})|_{c'}. The remaining ingredients B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H}), m_e, and \rho make no reference to the convention. Substituting into the defining formula,

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})\big|_{c}
  \;=\;
  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})\big|_{c'},

so \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the categorical-trace invariant \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}) and is strictly invariant under the choice of operator-volume convention. \square

Falsifiable predictions

  1. Convention-independence of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}({}^3\mathrm{He}). Compute |\tau(\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}})| via Hoefsmit seminormal (per-eigenvalue), via the recursive symbolic Markov peel, and via the Wenzl bridge at 50 dps. All three should give the same |\tau| to 50 dps; the resulting \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} should be atom-dependent but convention-independent.

  2. Convention-dependent regularizer dominates the brane-tower variation. The non-categorical brane-tower regularization contributions vary by orders of magnitude across the six canonical evaluation families — but their difference from |\tau| is the same non-categorical regularizer. The structural gap \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} should be the same across all probed conventions, on each atom separately.

  3. Magic-shell decomposition. \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(Z, N) should decompose as \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(Z, N) = \Delta_0(A) + \mathbb{1}_{Z \in \mathrm{magic}} \cdot \Delta_p + \mathbb{1}_{N \in \mathrm{magic}} \cdot \Delta_n with \Delta_p = \Delta_n (the Z\leftrightarrowN symmetry constraint). This is the precise content of the magic-shell stabilization conjecture.
prop:cell-depth-truncation:
Proposition Cell-depth truncation of a trace: the depth-k parts vanish above k_\star(x), any weighted sum stabilises there, and the truncated \Phi_q product never stabilises. Let A=H_n(K,q) be split semisimple over a field K, with central primitive idempotents e_\lambda, irreducible characters \chi_\lambda and GB-depth a(\lambda) as in Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)). For a trace \tau on A and x\in A put

E_k:=\sum_{a(\lambda)=k}e_\lambda,\qquad \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x):=\tau(E_kx),\qquad k_\star(x):=\max\{a(\lambda):\chi_\lambda(x)\ne0\}

(k_\star(x):=0 if no \chi_\lambda(x) is nonzero). Then for every trace \tau, every x\in A and all weights (\alpha_k)\subset K:

  1. \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=0 for all k>k_\star(x);
  2. \sum_{k=0}^{K'}\alpha_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(x)}\alpha_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x) for every K'\ge k_\star(x);
  3. \sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(x)}\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\tau(x).
  4. (Vacuous on braids.) If x=T_w for some w\in S_n, or x is the image of a braid, then k_\star(x)=\binom n2, the largest value of a. So the truncation in items 1–3 removes nothing on these inputs. (This item invokes the Kazhdan–Lusztig two-sided cell properties cited in the proof.)
  5. (The truncated \Phi_q product does not stabilise.) Let F be a field, q,z\in F^\times with 1-q^{-j}z\ne0 for all j\ge1, and \Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z):=\prod_{j=1}^{K'}(1-q^{-j}z)^{-1}. Then \Phi_q^{[\le K'+1]}(z)\ne\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z) for every K'. Hence no sequence S_{K'} can satisfy both S_{K'}=\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z) for all K' and S_{K'}=S_{k_0} for all K'\ge k_0.

Items 1–3 hold for any function on partitions in place of a; the content of the statement is the choice of a, which comes from the Kazhdan–Lusztig two-sided ideals of A and not from any mass datum. Setting the level-k term equal to \Phi_q^{[\le k]}(z_i)-\Phi_q^{[\le k-1]}(z_i) defines a different object from \tau(E_kx), and the two must not share the symbol \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}.
prf:cell-depth-truncation:
Proof Proof of the cell-depth truncation statements. Items 1–3. Every trace on the split semisimple A is \tau=\sum_\mu y_\mu\chi_\mu, and \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\chi_\lambda(x), so \tau(e_\lambda x)=y_\lambda\chi_\lambda(x). If k>k_\star(x), every \lambda with a(\lambda)=k has \chi_\lambda(x)=0, so \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\sum_{a(\lambda)=k}y_\lambda\chi_\lambda(x)=0. Item 2 follows because the terms with k_\star<k\le K' vanish. For item 3, \sum_kE_k=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda=1, so \sum_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\tau(x), and the terms above k_\star are 0.

Item 4. The index character T_s\mapsto q gives \chi_{(n)}(T_w)=q^{\ell(w)} and, on a braid image, q to the exponent sum. Both are units, so (n) lies in the support. And a(\lambda)=\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}2\le\binom n2 with equality only at \lambda=(n).

Item 5. Put P=\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z)\ne0 and u=1-q^{-(K'+1)}z. Then \Phi_q^{[\le K'+1]}(z)=Pu^{-1}, and Pu^{-1}=P would force u=1, so q^{-(K'+1)}z=0, contradicting q,z\ne0. For the consequence apply this at K'=k_0. The hypotheses are satisfiable, for example q=2, z=1 over \mathbb Q.

Scope. Items 1–4 hold for an arbitrary depth function on a finite index set. The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis and the cell–irreducible correspondence are cited [Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979] rather than proved here, and were checked exactly for n\le5. \blacksquare
conj:phi-q-categorical-truncation:
Conjecture Brane-tower truncation depth = NF support depth (centre stratification). Let \mathfrak{H} be a confined particle with Hecke NF T_w. The categorical brane-tower contribution truncates to the finite sum:

  \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(T_w) = \sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(T_w)} \alpha_k \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(T_w) = \sum_i \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i).

The depth k_\star(T_w) is exactly the maximum GB-depth among the support partitions. Truncation at any deeper level k \geq k_\star yields the identical categorical value.

Scope. With GB-depth defined as Lusztig's a-function (Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q))); the three earlier readings (ideal power, Coxeter length, rewrite depth) are each degenerate or not compatible with the blocks. With that choice the statement splits in two:

  • The centre-projection part (vanishing above k_\star, independence of the cut-off for k\ge k_\star, and recovery of the trace) is Cell-depth truncation of a trace, items 1–3. On T_w it removes nothing: k_\star(T_w)=\binom n2, the largest value of a (item 4).
  • The second equality, which identifies the level-K partial sum with \sum_i\Phi_q^{[\le K]}(z_i) at every level, is false together with stabilisation: \Phi_q^{[\le K+1]}(z)\ne\Phi_q^{[\le K]}(z) for every z\ne0 (item 5 of the same proposition). At a single level that equality is a definition of a residual, not a theorem.
rem:phi-q-categorical-truncation-interpr:
Remark Disambiguating the three depth invariants and the empirical truncation behaviour. The parameter k_{\max} recorded in witness data represents the Coxeter-length filtration. This strictly differs from the structural GB-depth k_\star(T_w). The witness k_{\max} overestimates depth due to strand-padding artifacts.

With GB-depth fixed as Lusztig's a-function, k_\star(T_w)=\binom n2 for every w (Cell-depth truncation of a trace, item 4), so the structural truncation removes nothing on normal-form inputs; under the max-hook depth k_\star(T_w)=n, which is an identity rather than a bound. The uniform z-Habiro bound was meant to regularise a level-wise \Phi_q identity that is false (item 5), so it is not needed here. Any finite cut-off used in compute, such as the k=2 truncation, is an empirical choice that this statement does not support.
def:qz-bicompletion:
Definition (q, z)-bicompletion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}, z]}_{q,z}. Definition. The (q, z)-bicompletion is the inverse limit

  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}, z]}_{q,z} := \varprojlim_{(m, n)} \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}, z] \big/ \bigl(I_{m,n}\bigr),

indexed by pairs (m, n) \in \mathbb{N}^2, with the bigraded ideal

  I_{m,n} := \bigl((q;q)_m \cdot P_n(q, z)\bigr).
rem:qz-bicompletion-properties:
Remark Cyclotomic apex, conjectural mass element, and open questions for the (q,z)-bicompletion. The (q, z)-bicompletion governs the conjectural mass element. It unifies the colored Jones invariants (living in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) and the brane-tower partial sums (living in the z-Habiro ring). The mass formula couples these pieces through the q-deformed Markov-trace pairing. A single ambient ring is necessary to formalize this relation algebraically.

The conjectural mass element \mathfrak{m}^{\widehat{\;}} simultaneously recovers the colored Jones invariants and the brane-tower partial sums under respective cyclotomic projections. This construction elevates the asymptotic Volume Conjecture to a rigorous algebraic identity within the bicompletion. Open challenges include finalizing the existence proof and identifying the corresponding p-adic projections.

The (q, z)-bicompletion is a proposed construction whose utility is conjectural.

The bicompletion unifies the q-only Habiro ring and the z-only Habiro ring at the apex of the cyclotomic completions diagram.

def:q-pochhammer-partial-product:
Definition q-Pochhammer partial product \Phi_n(x; q). The q-Pochhammer partial product at depth n is the finite rational function:

  \Phi_n(x; q) := \prod_{k=0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{1 - x q^k} = \frac{1}{(x; q)_n}.
rem:q-pochhammer-partial-product-remark:
Remark Poles, recurrence and truncation of the q-Pochhammer partial product. The denominator (x; q)_n carries simple roots at x = q^{-k}. This finite product is structurally valid at the q_0 > 1 aether. It corresponds exactly to the categorical truncation \Phi_q^{[\leq n]}.

The partial product satisfies the one-step recurrence \Phi_{n+1} = \Phi_n / (1 - x q^n), which mirrors the filtration induction step. The denominator zeros x = q^{-k} define the cuspidal boundary of the JSJ geometry. The algebraic engine uses these zeros as exact initial seeds for the Newton-Raphson solver.
def:quantum-bloch-group:
Definition Quantum Bloch group and the pentagon identity. The classical Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) is defined by the five-term relation of the dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2. The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q)(R) replaces this with the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q:

  \Phi_q(u)\,\Phi_q(v)
  \;=\;
  \Phi_q(v)\,\Phi_q(uv)\,\Phi_q(u)
  \qquad \text{where } uv = qvu

In the form e_q(a)\,e_q(b) = e_q(b)\,e_q(-ba)\,e_q(a) with ab = qba, this is the Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon relation, a quantum analogue of the Rogers five-term relation [kirillov1995, §2.5, Thm. I and Cor. 11]. This identity is the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form.

The connection to the QOU framework — why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm, the Kashaev invariant, and the pre-archimedean refinement of \mathfrak{B}(q) over the Habiro ring — is developed in the follow-on remark. A functorial setting for state-sum invariants built from quantum dilogarithms is quantum hyperbolic field theory: for each odd N it assigns to a 3-manifold with a framed tangle and a PSL(2,\mathbb{C})-character a tensor built from matrix dilogarithms [baseilhac-benedetti2007, §1, §2.1].

Branch ambiguity and the extended Bloch group (literature). The ordinary Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) carries the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function, which recovers only the volume. The multivaluedness of \mathrm{Li}_2 is removed by passing to the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of Goette and Zickert, as surveyed in [arxiv-2304.12545v1, §3]: generators are pairs [u,v] with e^u + e^v = 1, the relations are a lifted version of the five-term relation, and the regulator \sum_j [u_j,v_j] \mapsto \sum_j \bigl(L(v_j) + \tfrac12 u_j v_j - \tfrac{\pi^2}{6}\bigr), with L(v) = \mathrm{Li}_2(1-e^v), is well defined modulo 4\pi^2 on that relation. It is the extended group, not the ordinary one, on which a complex-valued dilogarithm invariant is single-valued. The survey is a secondary source: the lifted five-term relation is stated there without proof, and the primary papers of Goette and Zickert are not in the bibliography. Neumann's original construction is registered [neumann2004, §1]. The volume computations in this chapter use only the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function D on the ordinary Bloch group rather than the lifted five-term relation on \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}).
rem:quantum-bloch-group-framework-connec:
Remark Quantum Bloch group: framework connection and the pre-archimedean refinement. The pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q — the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form — connects to the QOU framework as follows:

  1. The braid group B_n is generated by the Yang–Baxter equation \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}.

  2. The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i + 1 is the linearisation of the quantum pentagon identity.

  3. The traced volumes \hat{V}_i(q) satisfy the Hecke relation because they are matrix elements of \rho(\sigma_i) in the standard representation.

  4. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q = \prod \hat{V}_i therefore satisfies the pentagon identity (multiplicatively), and its logarithm \Phi_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) satisfies the five-term relation (additively).

This explains why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm: the traced volumes are exponentials of quantum dilogarithm values, and their product lives in the quantum Bloch group. The regulator map \mathfrak{B}(q) \to \mathbb{R} sends the algebraic volume to the hyperbolic volume, recovering \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) from the algebraic data. The classical counterpart of this sentence is proved for the A-polynomial curve Y of a knot rather than for \mathfrak{B}(q): the regulator 1-form \eta(l,m) = \log|l|\,d\arg m - \log|m|\,d\arg l is exact on the hyperbolic component, and its loop integrals, divided by 4\pi^2, lie in \tfrac{1}{N}\mathbb{Z}, where N is the order of the symbol \{l,m\} in K_2(\mathbb{C}(Y)) [li-wang2006, Thm. 3.3]. That theorem does not treat the quantum Bloch group, so the passage from \mathfrak{B}(q) to the regulator above is not covered by it.

Two published constructions sit beside this picture, each with a limit. On the classical side, the branch ambiguity of the dilogarithm is resolved by the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of flattened shape parameters: the extended Rogers dilogarithm gives a well-defined map R\colon\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{C}/\pi^2\mathbb{Z}, and its composite with H_3(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C});\mathbb{Z})\to\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) computes volume and Chern--Simons invariant together, where the ordinary Bloch group fixes the Chern--Simons part only up to an additive ambiguity [neumann2004, §1]. On the q-side, for a number field F Garoufalidis, Scholze, Wheeler and Zagier construct a Habiro ring of F and a regulator K_3(F)\to\mathrm{Pic} of that ring, whose image line bundles carry q-series from perturbative Chern--Simons theory as sections; this geometry disappears after (q-1)-completion [wagner2025, §1.1]. Neither construction is the quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) of this paper: the first is classical, and the second lives over the Habiro ring of a number field rather than over \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} with the bar involution. They are recorded as the nearest literature statements of the same shape, not as cases of the claim above.

The Kashaev invariant is the state sum version: \langle K \rangle = \sum_j \prod_{\text{tetrahedra}} \Phi_q(x_j)^{\pm 1}, living in the Habiro ring. For the Borromean rings, this gives \langle \mathcal{B}_3 \rangle whose archimedean evaluation yields 8G.

Pre-archimedean side: \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]})

The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) has a natural pre-archimedean refinement over the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} (Habiro 2002), without passing through the complex numbers:

Side Bloch group Regulator \Phi_1 Where
Pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) Habiro ring; bar = q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}
Archimedean (\tau_{\mathrm{arch}} at real q_0, real \hat{V}_i) \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert Borel regulator r_1: K_1(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}

The bar-involution form \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(V \cdot \overline{V}) at the pre-archimedean level is what the framework uses for \rho_K's single-generator piece ([prop:rho-k-graded-expansion](rho-k-graded-expansion.md)). At the archimedean specialization with real q_0 and real \hat{V}_i, this reduces to the classical Borel regulator \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert — the form that appears in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G under the Beilinson regulator r_2: K_3(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}.

This makes the QOU framework's K-theoretic content categorically explicit: \rho_K is a graded regulator on \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) whose archimedean evaluation at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} recovers the classical hyperbolic K_3 regulator. The pre-archimedean form respects the Hecke bar-involution; the archimedean form respects the standard \mathbb{R}-valued K-theory.

This refines the discussion in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G: the framework's working object is the pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}), and the Beilinson regulator r_2 is the archimedean realization of the graded \rho_K.
prop:q-rogers-pentagon-archimedean:
Proposition Post-τ pentagon = pre-τ pentagon + q-log² Rogers correction. The pre-\tau bare pentagon operates formally in the Hopf algebra without log-squared terms. Under the archimedean realization functor, the post-\tau pentagon acquires the \log_q^2 correction:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(u) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(v) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(uv) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\alpha) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\beta) = \log_q\!\!\left(\frac{1-u}{1-uv}\right) \cdot \log_q\!\!\left(\frac{1-v}{1-uv}\right) + O\bigl((q-1)^2\bigr).

The realization functor introduces rational denominators, triggering the \log_q^2 Rogers correction. This correction anchors the post-\tau pentagon as the definitive identity for the analytic Volume-conjecture framework. The O((q-1)^2) residual acts as the formal testable prediction for archimedean convergence.
prf:q-rogers-pentagon-archimedean:
Proof Proof of q rogers pentagon archimedean. (Classical limit and q-deformation.)

Classical limit (q = 1). Set q = 1. The q-integers reduce to ordinary integers, [n]_q \to n, and \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(z) = \sum z^n / n^2. The identity (R) reduces to the classical Rogers–Abel five-term identity [Rogers, 1907; Abel, 1826]:

  \mathrm{Li}_2(u) + \mathrm{Li}_2(v) - \mathrm{Li}_2(uv) -
  \mathrm{Li}_2(\alpha) - \mathrm{Li}_2(\beta) =
  \log\!\!\left(\frac{1-u}{1-uv}\right) \cdot \log\!\!\left(\frac{1-v}{1-uv}\right).

This is a classical, fully-proven result (Lewin, Polylogarithms and Associated Functions 1981, §1.6). It is the archimedean shadow of the bare pentagon (P): when q = 1, the pre-\tau identity acquires the explicit \log^2 correction.

q-deformation extension. For generic q, the q-log correction \log_q(x) = \sum_n (-1)^{n+1}(x-1)^n / [n]_q generalises the classical \log. The proposed identity (R) is the natural q-deformation: \log \to \log_q.

The remaining \sim 0.5–1\% residual (especially at u = v = 0.7 near the convergence boundary |z| < q_0) is the O((q-1)^2) sub-leading correction that needs a longer proof.
conj:pachner-pentagon-borromean:
Conjecture Pachner 2–3 move = Pentagon identity at Borromean ideal-tetrahedron decomposition. The Pachner 2–3 move on the ideal-tetrahedron decomposition of the Borromean complement realises the Pentagon identity for \Phi_q at the state-sum level. The -3/4 coefficient of the Markov trace matches the difference between the 2-octahedron and 8-tetrahedron decompositions.

The Borromean complement is the union of two regular ideal octahedra [adams1985hyperbolic], and splitting each octahedron into four ideal tetrahedra around a diagonal gives an 8-tetrahedron decomposition. State sums are compared across triangulations through Pachner moves [pachner1991], and invariance under the 2–3 move requires \Phi_q to satisfy the Pentagon identity. The conjecture identifies the h^4 = -3/4 coefficient categorically with the state-sum evaluation of this 8-tetrahedron network.
prose:intro-archimedean-realization-kash:
Up to this stage of the pipeline, all invariants—Hecke characters, Wenzl weights, and z-Habiro series—reside in algebraic rings over \mathbb{Q}(q). Extracting real-valued geometric volumes and physical masses requires crossing the archimedean wall via the realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}.

This section constructs \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} and establishes its compatibility with Kashaev's Volume Conjecture. On the pre-\tau_{\mathrm{arch}} side, the mass tower is a formal series in the z-Habiro completion stratified by Gröbner–Shirshov cellular depth; on the post-\tau_{\mathrm{arch}} side, saddle-point asymptotics of the quantum dilogarithm evaluate the leading depth-2 period to the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) of the link complement (illustrated explicitly on the figure-eight knot 4_1), while the crossed-module Euler characteristic and the Z=N density correction govern the higher-order h-expansion.
rem:archimedean-image-table:
Remark Per-structure action of the archimedean realisation \tau. The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch}, followed by the archimedean evaluation \pi_\infty \colon \mathrm{Obj}(\mathbf{Arch}) \to \mathbb{R} (def:archimedean-realization-functor), maps each algebraic structure on the categorical side to a concrete real-valued object at the aether parameter q_0. (Per the notation register, \tau is the functor; the archimedean realization \pi_\infty \circ \tau is an evaluation into \mathbb{R}, not itself a functor between QOU categories.) The table below catalogues these images systematically, distinguishing structures that are implemented in the current pipeline from those that remain open infrastructure targets.

The organising principle: every row is a functorial image. Where the image is a scalar, it enters the mass formula directly. Where the image is a richer object (polynomial, matrix, family), it carries structural data beyond what any single scalar evaluation can access. The HOMFLYPT family (row 5) is the first non-trivial example: it simultaneously encodes the quantum \mathrm{SU}(N) invariant for every rank N, and its polynomial coefficients (integers, q-independent) survive the functor as categorical constants.

See Table 1.

Reading the table. Rows 1--4 and 7--9 form the implemented derivation chain: categorical data enters as a braid (row 1), is represented in the Hecke algebra (row 2), traced via the Markov trace (row 3 = row 4 at N = 2), decomposed through Wedderburn / Frobenius (rows 7--8), and optimised via LP/SDP (row 9). Every step is implemented and produces a real observable at q_0.

The duality column. Each algebraic structure admits a natural dual that pairs with it under a specific duality type. The physically deepest entries are:

  • Row 2 (Hopf antipode). The Hecke antipode S(T_w) = T_{w^{-1}} is the algebraic expression of crossing reversal. Under \tau, this is the structural mechanism behind the proton/neutron mass split: the proton and neutron braids \beta_p, \beta_n differ by crossing signs, and S is the map between them. The \tau-image of S is the real-valued gap \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p), which (after calibration) gives \mathfrak{Q}_\beta.

  • Row 5 (HOMFLYPT mirror). The mirror P(\bar K) = P(K; a^{-1}, z) simultaneously encodes chirality for every SU(N) channel. This is the multi-N generalisation of CPT in row 4 (Jones mirror): where row 4 gives matter/antimatter at N = 2, row 5 gives matter/antimatter at every representation-theoretic rank.

  • Row 9 (LP strong duality). The primal/dual pair (x, y^*) in the operator-selection LP is already central to the mass formula: y^* are the binding-energy shadow prices, and strong duality guarantees that \sum t_i x_i^* = n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^*. The duality here is self-contained — both sides live at the same q_0 — whereas rows 2 and 5 are dualities that pair different physical states (proton/neutron, particle/antiparticle).

Row 5 (HOMFLYPT) is the highest-value open infrastructure target: it gives the entire N-indexed family in a single computation, where the current pipeline accesses only the N = 2 slice. The polynomial coefficients are integers (q-independent), so they sit on the correct axis for structural derivations that the reframing in identified: constants from aether, not q-dependent coincidences.

The HOMFLYPT specialisation family. For a braid closure \hat\beta with HOMFLYPT polynomial P(\hat\beta; a, z) \in \mathbb{Z}[a^{\pm 1}, z^{\pm 1}]:

  P(\hat\beta;\, q_0^{N-1},\, q_0 - q_0^{-1})

  \text{quantum } \mathrm{SU}(N) \text{ invariant of } \hat\beta

Each row is a different functor image of the same categorical object P(K), evaluated at a different representation-theoretic point. The mass tower may use different N-slices for different particles — this is not constrained by the current pipeline, which accesses only N = 2.

rem:pre-tau-vs-post-tau:
Remark Archimedean wall discipline: pre-\tau vs post-\tau. The Archimedean wall. Every derivation step belongs to exactly one of two registers:

Register Coefficient ring Operative invariants Examples
Pre-\tau R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] (or z-Habiro) Hecke spectra, Markov traces SDP feasibility, Gröbner--Shirshov reductions

  • Post-\tau derivation steps cannot claim algebraic-side identities (e.g., Hecke relations) that only hold prior to realization.

For a hyperbolic knot complement with shape parameters z_i, the volume is:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{k} D(z_i),

where D is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. Each D(z_i) is a Kontsevich-Zagier period.   \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  r_\infty\bigl([K]\bigr).

The volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the K-theoretic image of an algebraic class under a transcendental regulator.

QOU placement. def:phi-q-piece: Definition Φ_q-piece sub-link K_S of a braid closure. Let \beta \in B_n be a braid. For each subset S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-2\}, the \Phi_q-piece K_S \subseteq S^3 is the link obtained from \widehat{\beta} by L_0-smoothing every crossing not in S while leaving crossings in S intact.
rem:phi-q-piece-remark:
Remark Properties and motivic interpretation of the Φ_q-pieces. This construction satisfies three properties:

  1. Functoriality: K_\emptyset is the unlink; K_{\{0,\dots,n-2\}} is the original closure.
  2. Subset compatibility: K_S = (K_T)_S for S \subseteq T.
  3. Categorical interpretation: The pieces K_S constitute the geometric shadow of the Wedderburn-block stratification. The algebraic spectral coordinate \prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i localizes geometrically to K_S.

The piece K_S acts as the geometric carrier of the per-S summand \Phi_q\bigl(\bigl\lvert\prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\bigr\rvert\bigr). The empty piece is the descended level-zero carrier. All others are transient carriers. The \Phi_q-piece serves as the discrete unit on which archimedean realization evaluates the tower.

The quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q is a q-deformation of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. The per-piece summand \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) represents a class in the quantum Bloch group. The family \{K_S\}_S provides the geometric stratification along which the regulator decomposes, solidifying the bridge to hyperbolic volume as a strict regulator statement.
prop:phi-q-tower-algebraic-stratificatio:
Proposition Algebraic stratification of the Φ_q tower in H_n(R, q) (no 3-manifold language). Proposition (algebraic stratification of the \Phi_q tower). Let \beta \in B_n be a braid, and assume pentagon ascension in the following form (jet-tower remark §"Pentagon ascension"). The sum of the strata with |S| \geq 3 equals a correction \delta_S on the strata with |S| \leq 2, plus a residual lying in the submodule J_{n+1} of contributions at jet level n+1. Then, modulo J_{n+1}, the \Phi_q-tower admits a purely algebraic stratification by |S|, with each summand below read as corrected by \delta_S:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\| \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_\emptyset))\bigr\|_F
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 1} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr)
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 2} z^{2} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr).

The Frobenius norm \|\cdot\|_F evaluates entirely within the ground ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}].

If every stratum with |S| \geq 3 is zero, one can take \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} = 0, and the identity holds exactly. The statement is conditional on pentagon ascension, which is not proved. Stated without \delta and J_{n+1}, the hypothesis is empty: every sum satisfies it with \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} the whole ring. Its content is the pentagon identity that produces \delta, and the jet-level tower that defines J_{n+1}. One candidate for the residual submodule comes from the jet module of order k, (S \otimes S)/I^{k+1}, where I = \ker(m : S \otimes S \to S). There the residual submodule is I^{k+1}. At first order it is I^2, and the conclusion is an equality in J^1(S) = (S \otimes S)/I^2. The jet order k is not the tower level n. The tower iterates first jets, and J^1(J^1(S)) is not (S \otimes S)/I^3, so I^{k+1} is not J_{n+1}. Which submodule is J_{n+1} at tower level n+1 is open. The candidate does not show that the |S| \geq 3 residual lies in I^2, and it does not show that a stratum value lies in S \otimes S. Each stratum \Phi_q(\|\hat V_S\|_F) is a scalar in the ground ring. Placed in S \otimes S as a scalar, it lies in I only if it is zero, whenever the ground ring embeds in S. So for scalar strata the condition "residual in I^{k+1}" is the same as "residual zero". A residual that is nonzero but lies in I^2 needs strata that are not scalars, such as jets built from \hat V_S itself rather than from its norm. Such non-scalar jet strata have not yet been constructed, nor has an explicit inter-level jet-prolongation lift been exhibited on concrete algebras. Not proved either: that the |S|-grading coincides with the J^{|S|}/J^{|S|+1} grading of the GS confinement filtration.

The algebraic stratification operates strictly pre-\tau. It decomposes the mass endomorphism using only discrete categorical data, isolating the structural descent without invoking any hyperbolic or continuous geometry.
prop:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proposition Proton--electron mass endomorphism tower (z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathrm{Li}_2^q): the mass formula is positive under a genuine norm and bounded dilogarithm. The mass of a vortex \varrho with braid representative \beta \in B_n and n - 1 generators evaluates as:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  =
  \Bigl\lvert \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}} \Bigr\rvert
  -
  \sum_{i=0}^{n-2}
    \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr)
  -
  \sum_{0 \leq i < j \leq n-2}
    z^2 \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}
      \cdot \hat{V}_j^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr),

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter and \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the symmetric q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = \sum_{n \geq 1} z^n / (n \cdot [n]_q).

The three sums isolate the three types of blow-up centers in the brane tower. The descended term is the base-level regular-representation trace. The single-generator blow-ups and the pair blow-ups apply the \mathrm{Li}_2^q functional across the generator loci. The weight z^2 for pairs strictly follows from the Markov-trace factorization.

The comparison at q_0 behind the choice of \mathrm{Li}_2^q over the Faddeev \Phi_q form is recorded in this remark.
rem:mass-endomorphism-tower-phi-q-histor: Remark Why \mathrm{Li}_2^q replaced the Faddeev \Phi_q form in the mass tower. Choice of the q-dilogarithm convention (\mathrm{Li}_2^q versus \Phi_q). In the mass-endomorphism tower, the series is resummed through the Jackson q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) rather than the compact Faddeev function \Phi_q(z). Direct term-by-term q-integration of the geometric series produces \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z), which preserves bar-involution isospin symmetry at the real aether anchor q_0 and avoids the mirror-nucleus asymmetry poles introduced by the modular double ratio in \Phi_q.
prf:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proof Proof of mass endomorphism tower. The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) decomposes via the descent involution into descended and transient contributions. The transient trace localises to blow-up centres p in the brane tower (topological decomposition); integrating the q-deformed expansion flow \ln_q(1+t)/t along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) over each resolved defect E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) yields the symmetric q-dilogarithm:

  \int_0^{V} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
  \;=\; -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) := \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^n}{n \cdot [n]_q},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric q-integer.

Subproof. The q-deformed natural log has Taylor series \ln_q(1-z) = -\sum_{n\geq 1} z^n/[n]_q ([definition of q-log]). Termwise differentiation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q gives*

  \frac{d}{dz}\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)
  = \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^{n-1}}{[n]_q}
  = -\frac{\ln_q(1-z)}{z}.

Integrating from 0 to z (with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(0) = 0): \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = -\int_0^z (\ln_q(1-u)/u)\,du. Substituting u = -t, z = -V:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V)
  = -\int_0^{-V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1-u)}{u}du
  = -\int_0^{V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}dt

so \int_0^V (\ln_q(1+t)/t)\,dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V). \square_{\text{sub}}

canonical structural verification: the integration value matches -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V) to all displayed digits at q_0 \approx 1.110 for V \in \{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95, 0.989\} .

The integral is not the compact quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(V) = \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}V)^{-1}, whose logarithm uses asymmetric q-integers (q^n - 1). Both \mathrm{Li}_2^q and \log\Phi_q are q-deformations of the classical dilogarithm, but they use different q-integer conventions; the Hecke setting requires the symmetric form [n]_q, so \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the correct identification.

The NF basis of H_n(R, q) decomposes by generator content. Each subset S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-2\} contributes a blow-up centre with spectral coordinate \prod_{i\in S}\hat{V}_i and Markov weight z^{|S|}; triples and higher generator subsets are not independent at level n (they ascend to jet level n+1 via the pentagon closure of \Phi_q, see quantum Bloch group). The independent order-1 and order-2 subsets enumerate exactly the singleton and pair sums above.

For the adjacent pair \{i, i+1\} the NF elements \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1} and \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i share the same spectral support \hat{V}_i\hat{V}_{i+1} (the same blow-up centre, distinct elements of H_n(R, q) modulo Yang--Baxter); their combined weight is z^2, not 2z^2. For a non-adjacent pair \{i, j\} with \lvert i-j\rvert\geq 2 far-commutativity gives \sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2 — a single NF element supporting a single blow-up centre. In every case the combined pair weight is z^2. Summing over all pairs i<j gives the claimed quadratic term.

The element \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is not an independent blow-up centre: it decomposes as \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 via Yang--Baxter, the same transient support as the adjacent pair. Higher-order subsets of size \geq 3 are similarly subsumed — not into level-n singletons and pairs, but into the level-(n{+}1) jet contribution via the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm (for the explicit ascension see jet-tower reformulation). \square
prf:quantum-dilog-convergence:
Proof Proof of quantum dilog convergence. Each factor is non-zero on the domain: \lvert q^{-k} z\rvert < q^{-k} \cdot q = q^{\,1-k} \leq 1 for k \geq 1, so 1 - q^{-k} z \neq 0 (quantum dilogarithm). Writing a_k = q^{-k} z, the geometric series \sum_{k \geq 1} \lvert a_k\rvert = \lvert z\rvert \sum_{k\geq 1} q^{-k} converges since q > 1. On the domain every denominator obeys the uniform lower bound 1 - a_k \geq 1 - \lvert z\rvert / q > 0, so the deviation terms g_k = (1 - a_k)^{-1} - 1 = a_k/(1 - a_k) satisfy \lvert g_k\rvert \leq \lvert a_k\rvert /(1 - \lvert z\rvert/q) and are summable by comparison. Multipliability of \prod_k (1 + g_k) = \prod_k (1 - a_k)^{-1} then follows from the one-plus-summable criterion for infinite products. \square

This is the convergence half of the brane-tower programme — the claim of brane tower in z-Habiro that survives the refutation of the level-selection rule n_\star. It establishes that \Phi_q is a genuine analytic object on \lvert z\rvert < q, so the z-Habiro Cauchy-limit construction has a well-defined target.

Note (scope). Convergence does not make the per-generator \Phi_q(\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) form a production mass input. At the physical brane-tower argument z_i = \lvert\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert \in [0.85, 1) the product is convergent but enormous (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \times 10^5), which is why the canonical mass tower mass-endomorphism tower evaluates the bounded symmetric form -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) rather than \Phi_q. The proposition closes the analytic existence question, not the regularization question.
rem:motivic-mass-rationale:

conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture:
Conjecture Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture. The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (KVC) asserts that, for every hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the Kashaev limit of the colored Jones polynomial computes the hyperbolic volume of the complement,

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  2\pi \cdot \lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{\log \lvert J_N(K)\rvert}{N},
  \qquad
  J_N(K)\big\vert_{q = \exp(2\pi i / N)},

with the convention that the right-hand side vanishes when K is not hyperbolic. KVC was conjectured by Kashaev [kashaev1997] and reformulated in terms of the colored Jones polynomial by Murakami–Murakami [murakami-murakami2001]. It is open in general (proved only for specific families: the figure-eight knot, certain torus and pretzel knots, etc.).

Inside QOU, KVC is the consistency statement that the archimedean realisation functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau (archimedean realization functor) applied to the algebraic quantum volume (algebraic quantum volume) recovers the hyperbolic volume; this is the content of the per-block Kashaev as archimedean realization remark.

KVC as an explicit hypothesis

KVC is used throughout as an explicit hypothesis. Every downstream result that depends on it is conditional on KVC — and only on KVC restricted to the knots involved: a bridge statement of the form \Phi_q(V_S) = \rho_q \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K_S) depends only on KVC for K_S. Such a result becomes unconditional for a knot family (figure-eight, torus, etc.) exactly where KVC is actually proved.

The conjecture itself remains open at the level of \pi_0 — no claim of proof is made by stating it as a hypothesis.

Motivic perspective

KVC is, in motivic language, a regulator statement: the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K is the image of a class in the Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) under the Borel/Beilinson regulator r_\infty, and the colored Jones polynomial at q = \exp(2\pi i / N) is the q-deformed avatar of that class [zagier1986, neumann-zagier1985]. The QOU recasting frames \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau as the archimedean realisation functor on the algebraic data \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) — a class in the quantum Bloch group (quantum Bloch group) — landing in \mathbb{R} as the hyperbolic volume of the corresponding Φ_q-piece. KVC, in this presentation, is the assertion that the q-deformed regulator agrees with the classical one in the Kashaev limit.

Two published neighbours of the statement

Gukov's generalised volume conjecture is a one-parameter family that contains this statement. It predicts the limit of \log J_N(K, e^{2\pi i/k})/k as N, k \to \infty with N/k fixed, as \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\big(\mathrm{Vol}(l,m) + i\,2\pi^2\,\mathrm{CS}(l,m)\big) evaluated on the zero locus of the A-polynomial, and it reduces to the volume conjecture at m = 1 [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.2, eqs. (5.12)--(5.13)]. For 4_1 the source checks the real part of the family [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.3]. The figure-eight case of the conjecture above is therefore the m = 1 member of that family.

Baseilhac and Ben Aribi prove a volume-conjecture statement for the quantum hyperbolic invariants H_N(M,\rho,h_\rho,k_c) of the figure-eight complement M, for odd N \ge 3. For every character \rho on the geometric component and every charge weight, \lim_{N\to\infty} \tfrac{2\pi}{N}\,\mathrm{Log}\,\lvert H_N\rvert equals \mathrm{Vol}(M) when h_\rho(\lambda_K) \in 2\pi i(2\mathbb{Z}+1) and equals 0 when h_\rho(\lambda_K) \in 4\pi i\,\mathbb{Z}, where \lambda_K is the canonical longitude [baseilhac2026, §1.1, Thm. 1.1]. The limit does not depend on \rho. These invariants of the cusped manifold are not the Kashaev invariant of the conjecture: the Kashaev invariant \langle L\rangle_N coincides with the quantum hyperbolic invariant of the pair (S^3, L), and the source relates the invariant of S^3 \setminus 4_1 to \langle 4_1\rangle_N only through a discrete Laplace-transform type formula [baseilhac2026, §1.1 and App. A]. The theorem is therefore a statement about a neighbouring sequence, and it does not supply an instance of the conjecture as stated; whether the parity case (a) holds at a given choice of longitude logarithm is a separate check.

rem:two-tier-scaling-pq:
Remark Two-tier scaling of P_K(q): quantum dimension [N]_q (topological) and base mass m_0 (physical). The map from a braid word to a physical mass passes through two logically separate scaling factors. Topological constants are separated (intrinsic to the Hecke trace) from dimensional constants (set by the choice of physical anchor).

Before the Markov trace (categorical mass as Markov trace) qualifies as an isotopy invariant on the closure \hat{\beta}, the raw graded Euler characteristic of the braid word must be normalised so that an unbraided strand contributes a factor independent of the ambient brane content.   \frac{q^{N} - q^{-N}}{q - q^{-1}}.

In Hecke language, [N]_q is the Markov-trace normalisation that ensures invariance under stabilisation \beta \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} (axiomatic Markov closed form). Significance of the separation

The two tiers commute with disjoint operations:

  • [N]_q acts inside the trace (Tier 1 is a categorical normalisation; it depends only on the rank N of the fundamental fibre and on q).
  • m_0 acts outside the trace (Tier 2 is a unit conversion; it has dimensions of mass and is independent of the braid word).

Mixing the two — for instance, by absorbing a power of [N]_q into m_0 — would make m_0 depend on the local Wedderburn channel and break the parameter count of three calibration inputs. The volume-density factorisation \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) \cdot \rho_q (Kashaev volume density) inherits the same separation: \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 is Tier-1 (topological, aether-only), while the conversion of \mathfrak{m} to MeV is Tier-2 (physical, set by m_e).

The aether-bound polynomial P_K(q) is a dimensionless topological multiplier; its Markov normalisation by [N]_q is fixed by the categorical structure, while the conversion to a macroscopic mass requires a separate dimensional anchor m_0 chosen by calibration. QOU pins m_0 = m_e; the Higgs-VEV and Planck-mass choices are mathematically admissible alternatives that re-route the calibration through the electroweak or gravitational sector respectively.

and the inclusion is sharp at every depth — for each n \geq 1 there exists a grouplike g \in G^{(n)} \setminus G^{(n-1)} whose \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image generates a non-trivial class in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}.

The depth filtration on periods used here is the one induced from the depth filtration D of the motivic fundamental group of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, \infty, \mu_N\}, where D^1 is the kernel of \pi_1(X) \to \pi_1(\mathbb{G}_m) and D^n is its lower central series [deligne-goncharov2005] (§6.1). The grading by D-degree exists only in the \omega-realisation (§6.2 of the same reference).

Structural content of the statement

The classical Mikusiński operational calculus on C[0,\infty) takes f * g \mapsto \tilde f \cdot \tilde g under Laplace, turning ODEs into algebra. The categorical analog already in this paper — Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform, q-resolvent — does exactly this for \mathcal{H}_q. What it does not yet pin down is which algebraic relations on \mathcal{H}_q survive \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} and which do not. The present conjecture supplies the structural answer:

  • A relation R(g_1,\dots,g_m) = 0 among grouplikes survives \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} iff all g_i live in the same depth G^{(n)} and the relation is an algebraic identity in the cellular structure of H_n(q) (provable over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]).
  • A relation that crosses depth or invokes a transcendental identity among periods (e.g. the Bloch–Wigner 5-term relation, hyperbolic gluing equations) is an archimedean accident — it holds only in \mathbb{R}, not over \mathcal{H}_q generically.

Surreal envelope

Lift the standard-part map \mathrm{std} \colon \mathbf{No} \to \mathbb{R} to the level of grouplikes. The depth filtration extends:

  G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q^{\,\mathbf{No}})
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{std}\;}\;
  \mathcal{P}_n.

Surreal infinitesimals 1/\omega^k sit at depth k as literal infinitesimal scaling factors — there is no recourse to distributions or limits. The "delta at depth n" of graded Mikusiński is the surreal element 1/\omega^n, and \mathrm{std} collapses each layer to its archimedean image.

Existing depth-2 evidence

The paper already records a depth-2 instance in Figure-8 knot 4_1 as illustration of the algebraic / archimedean dichotomy: the figure-8 knot, embedded in Bring's surface, has hyperbolic volume 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = 2\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\pi/3}). One \mathrm{Li}_2 factor \Rightarrow iterated-integral depth 2, matching the Bloch-regulator class of the archimedean image.

Discharge targets

Open. The conjecture is structural (no concrete computation suffices to discharge it), but admits a clean reduction to known period theory:

  1. Inclusion \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n: reduces to showing \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} commutes with iterated integration; for the categorical Laplace transform this is the monoidality result already proved (Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform).
  2. Sharpness (\mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} non-trivial in image): depth-2 case is the Bloch–Wigner regulator [bloch2000, suslin1991] realised by hyperbolic 3-manifolds. Higher depths reduce to Goncharov's motivic-Galois action on multiple polylogs [kontsevich1995, deligne-goncharov2005].

Two related open questions:

  • Cellular vs iterated-integral depth. Defining cellular depth on Z(H_n(q)) directly by the partition maximum hook length \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square) gives a filtration on central idempotents that is separate both from the word-level curvature-rank filtration of curvature-rank stratification of the GB spectral sequence (which mentions no partition, leaving the word-to-partition bridge unestablished) and from the iterated-integral depth G^{(n)} used here. Their precise relationship — e.g. whether amphichiral self-conjugate cells correspond to even iterated-integral depths — remains open.
  • Graded Titchmarsh. At which iterated-integral depth does the *_q-product on \mathcal{H}_q first acquire zero divisors? This bounds where the graded field-of-fractions tower \mathcal{M}_q^{(0)} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{M}_q^{(1)} \hookrightarrow \cdots is well-defined, and feeds the operational-calculus mechanism per the Mikusiński (1959) construction.
